key_insight: A tunable methylammonium polybromide melt can directly convert elemental metal films into optoelectronic-grade bromide perovskites in one room-temperature, solvent-free step.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable, roll-to-roll-compatible route for fabricating perovskite and perovskite-related films from metal precursors while reducing process complexity and stability constraints.
method: Use methylammonium polybromide melt (PBM) as the reactive medium
React PBM directly with elemental metals such as Pb, Sn, Au, and Cu at room temperature
Tune PBM composition to control oxidation state and suppress unwanted overoxidation, especially for Sn
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful conversion of multiple metals into MAPbBr3, MASnBr3, MA2Au2Br6, and MA2CuBr4, with in situ X-ray diffraction observing transient intermediates in two cases.
watch_item: Reaction outcomes depend on metal redox chemistry and PBM composition, so process control is needed to avoid overoxidation or unintended phases.
paper_title: A Universal Polybromide Melt Strategy for the Direct Conversion of Metals into Optoelectronic-Grade Bromide Perovskites
